movie_title: Will there be another pandemic in your lifetime?
introduction: Explore the probability of a future pandemic and the steps we can take to reduce its destructiveness

vocabulary.definition: widespread occurrence of a disease affecting a whole country or the world
vocabulary.example: The 1918 flu pandemic had devastating effects on the global population.

vocabulary.definition: a bacterium, virus, or other microorganism that can cause disease
vocabulary.example: Scientists are studying the pathogen responsible for the new outbreak.

vocabulary.definition: a place where a pathogen normally lives and multiplies
vocabulary.example: The jungle serves as a reservoir for many infectious diseases.

vocabulary.definition: the ability of an organism to resist a particular infection or toxin by the action of specific antibodies or sensitized white blood cells
vocabulary.example: Vaccinations help to build immunity against certain diseases.

vocabulary.definition: the transfer of a pathogen from one species to another
vocabulary.example: The spillover of the virus from bats to humans led to the current pandemic.

vocabulary.definition: the extent to which something is probable; the likelihood of something happening or being the case
vocabulary.example: The probability of a severe earthquake in this region is very low.
